correctness.rationale: The composition of integer maps T_m(x)={mx} is multiplication by the product of sampled slopes mod 1 and uniform Lebesgue initial law remains invariant under each map. Direct inverse-branch integration gives L_m(x-1/2)=(x-1/2)/m, so for lag k the covariance equals (12)^(-1) pi(P_t D)^k 1 and is summable. Two-by-two inversion of the Green–Kubo series yields the exact stated sigma_t^2, H=det(I-P_tD)>0, and symbolic differentiation verifies d sigma_t^2/dt=(d-e)^2/(12 H^2), including the equal-slope flat case. Variation contraction and mixing of the two-state driver give ergodicity; the reversed-chain bounded solution (I-DP_t)^(-1)1 to the Poisson equation yields a bounded martingale decomposition and functional CLT. At t=1, frozen random slope yields the half-half normal mixture, non-Gaussian if a!=b. Independently verified the rational derivative identity for all symbolic d,e, and (a,b)=(2,3) variance (12-7t)/(12(5-3t)), with endpoints 17/84 and 5/24. Finite algebra is a supplement, not an infinite FCLT proof.
